newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania government approves draft of mining reform.
newsitem.headline: Romania government approves draft of mining reform.

text.p: The Romanian government has approved the draft of a mining law expected to put local and foreign investors on equal footing and end the state monopoly in the sector, the industry minister said on Friday.
"The new law will grant an indiscriminatory treatment to all operators who own exploration and exploitation licences," Industry Minister Calin Tariceanu said at a news conference.
To be put into effect, the bill must be endorsed by parliament.
Under the bill, the licences would be issued by the National Agency for Mineral Resources (ANRM), an independent body in charge of the mineral rights administration, he said.

"We want to put an end to the situations when the state was both a referee and a player," Tariceanu said in reference to the independently run state-owned companies in the sector, which have been so far the recipients of the licences issued by the government.
He said the bill would allow the agency to issue licences for concessions on mining sites for up to 20 years to both Romanian and foreign operators.
The law is in line with efforts by the new centrist government, headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, to amend the present legislation and make investment more attractive to foreigners.
Last year, Romania's parliament passed a new petroleum law which operators said was "liberal and workable."
"We hope to have the first contracts signed within the next four months," Tariceanu said.
